ei.title: The Role of Order in Effective Teaching
ei.subject: 수능특강

fullPassage:
[1번] Teaching reflects what society itself demands; it necessitates that disorder — of students and teachers alike, of mind, behavior, and environment — yield to its opposite. Effective teaching requires that, failing their own self-imposed order, students experience the imposition of some outer order so that inner order may develop. This means in practice, for instance, that the goals of classes and courses be clearly set, that they be explained and justified, that the manner of achieving them be clear, that the presentation of materials conducive to reaching them be appropriate, and that all activities be directed somehow to their attainment. It means, too, that students take up their own obligation to maintain the conditions under which learning occurs: quiet in their classrooms, respect for and courtesy toward others, civility of language and behavior, and the like. Above all, it implies structured industry — study and activity that are oriented toward a goal and pursued with perseverance and method. That is, good teaching requires that teachers and students subject themselves to external and internal control so that learning can take place.

[2번] When we lecture, scold, yell, or criticize, when we say something positive but in a sarcastic tone, or when we try to make our kids feel guilty, it activates their amygdala, triggering their stress response and putting them into a defensive, rigid, reactive state. Even more basic, when we say no or don't, it releases stress chemicals in our kids' brains (and in ours) that are associated with fear and anger. Functional brain imaging research has shown that even seeing the word no on a screen for less than a second while you're lying in an MRI scanner will cause your brain to suddenly release dozens of stress-producing hormones and neurotransmitters. Conversely, positive words like yes, love, and peace activate systems in the prefrontal cortex that are related to emotional regulation. The problem is that negative words like no and don't have a more powerful effect on kids than positive words. For this reason, the researchers Suniya Luthar and John Gottman say that "bad is stronger than good" when it comes to communicating with children and teens.

[3번] The experiences of learning to ride a bicycle or drive a car illustrate well how the "what" and "how" systems — those involved in object identification and practical action — might interact during development. When we learn to drive a car, we go through a first stage where each required action and sequence of actions — such as looking in the mirror, signaling with the blinker, pressing the clutch prior to shifting into gear, and so forth — are explicitly thought of and double-checked while monitoring our situation in the environment. Once learned and after a few hours of practice, the required actions for driving become second nature, transferable to almost any vehicle and performed without explicit thinking. Information appears to be perceived directly; the affordances of the road, the car, and the traffic implicitly detected. Actually, this sort of automatization of conscious learning can be jeopardized by the return of explicit awareness. If you start to think too much about your driving, you actually increase your chances of having an accident. People in sport competitions confirm that self-consciousness is one's worst enemy: tennis, golf, or billiard players commonly report that they lose their "touch" by thinking too much about their moves.

[Gateway] The purpose of class discussions is to encourage you to be an active participant, not a passive recorder. Much of the emphasis in a discussion is on getting students involved in thinking, reacting, and responding. These are important intellectual activities in the learning process, for through them you are supposed to discover and express your opinions. Writing is an invaluable tool for accomplishing these tasks. Unfortunately, too many times, when class discussion begins, pens and pencils go down. Admittedly, it is considerably more difficult to take notes from discussions than from lectures, for, unlike lectures, discussions tend to be disorganized and difficult to follow. Also, students usually don't know how much of what other students are saying is important. And if you are an active participant, it is not easy to take notes and formulate what you want to say. But note taking in discussions is not only manageable, it is also important. Note taking helps to keep you active and alert; it allows you to impose some organization on the discussion; and it can prepare you to speak.

det.korean: 야단과 비꼼은 아이들을 방어적·반응적 상태로 몰아 스트레스 반응을 유발하고, 'no'나 'don't'는 두려움·분노와 관련된 화학물질을 분비시킨다. 부정적 말은 긍정적 말보다 강력한 효과를 가진다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① guilty: '죄책감을 느끼게 하다'는 부정적 의사소통의 예로 문맥에 적절
✅ ② stress: 편도체 활성화가 유발하는 것은 '스트레스 반응'이므로 문맥에 적절
❌ ③ peace → fear: 뒤에 이어지는 and anger와 짝을 이루어야 하므로 '두려움(fear)'이 적절. '평화(peace)'는 화학물질이 분노와 관련된다는 맥락과 모순
✅ ④ negative: 긍정적 말보다 더 강력한 효과를 미친다는 주장은 '부정적' 말에 대한 것이므로 적절
det.tip: and로 연결된 병렬 구조(fear and anger)는 같은 정서 방향(부정적)이어야 합니다. peace는 긍정어 군집(yes, love, peace)에 속합니다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 학급 토론의 목적은 수동적 기록자가 아닌 능동적 참여자가 되도록 너를 격려하는 것이다. 토론에서 강조되는 많은 부분은 학생들이 생각하고 반응하고 응답하는 것에 참여하게 만드는 것이다. 이러한 일들을 이루는 데에 있어 글쓰기는 매우 귀중한 도구이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① to encourage: be동사 is의 보어로 쓰인 to부정사로 올바른 어법
❌ ② get → getting: 전치사 on의 목적어 자리이므로 동명사 getting이 와야 함. 동사원형 get은 전치사의 목적어가 될 수 없어 부적절
✅ ③ to discover: be supposed to 뒤의 동사원형 discover로 올바른 어법
✅ ④ accomplishing: 전치사 for 뒤에 동명사 accomplishing이 와서 올바른 어법
det.tip: 전치사(on, for, of, in 등) 뒤에는 동명사(V-ing)가 와야 합니다. 동사원형은 전치사의 목적어가 될 수 없습니다.

questions.passage: [3번] The experiences of learning to ride a bicycle or drive a car illustrate well how the "what" and "how" systems — those ①<u>involved</u> in object identification and practical action — might interact during development. When we learn ②<u>to drive</u> a car, we go through a first stage ③<u>which</u> each required action and sequence of actions — such as looking in the mirror, signaling with the blinker, pressing the clutch prior to shifting into gear, and so forth — are explicitly thought of and double-checked while ④<u>monitoring</u> our situation in the environment. Once learned and after a few hours of practice, the required actions for driving become second nature, transferable to almost any vehicle and performed without explicit thinking. Information appears to be perceived directly; the affordances of the road, the car, and the traffic implicitly detected. Actually, this sort of automatization of conscious learning can be jeopardized by the return of explicit awareness. If you start to think too much about your driving, you actually increase your chances of having an accident. People in sport competitions confirm that self-consciousness is one's worst enemy: tennis, golf, or billiard players commonly report that they lose their "touch" by thinking too much about their moves.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: '무엇(what)' 체계와 '어떻게(how)' 체계 — 대상 식별과 실제 행동에 관여하는 체계들 — 는 발달 과정에서 상호작용할 수 있다. 우리가 차 운전을 배울 때, 우리는 각 행동과 일련의 행동들이 명시적으로 생각되고 이중 점검되는 첫 단계를 거친다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① involved: 앞의 those(= the "what" and "how" systems)를 수식하는 과거분사로 수동 의미(~에 관여된)를 나타내는 올바른 어법
✅ ② to drive: learn의 목적어로 쓰인 to부정사 명사적 용법으로 올바른 어법
❌ ③ which → where: 뒤에 완전한 절 'each required action... are explicitly thought of...'이 이어지고 선행사가 stage(추상적 단계·장소)이므로 관계부사 where가 와야 함. 관계대명사 which는 뒤에 불완전한 절이 오므로 부적절
✅ ④ monitoring: while 뒤의 분사구문(we are monitoring에서 being 생략)으로 올바른 어법
det.tip: 선행사가 장소·시간·이유·방법을 나타내고 뒤에 완전한 절이 오면 관계부사, 불완전한 절이 오면 관계대명사를 씁니다.

det.korean: 강조되는 많은 부분은 학생들을 생각, 반응, 응답에 참여시키는 것이다. 이러한 지적 활동을 통해 너는 자신의 의견을 발견하고 표현하게 된다. 글쓰기는 이러한 일을 이루는 데 매우 귀중한 도구이다. 유감스럽게도, 학급 토론이 시작되면 펜과 연필이 내려간다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① involved: get + 과거분사 구문으로 수동의 의미를 나타내는 올바른 어법
✅ ② through: '~을 통해'라는 의미의 전치사로 올바른 어법
❌ ③ invaluably → invaluable: be동사 is 뒤 명사 tool을 수식하는 자리이므로 형용사 invaluable이 와야 함. 부사 invaluably는 명사를 수식할 수 없어 부적절
✅ ④ when: '~할 때'라는 시간의 접속사로 올바른 어법
det.tip: 명사를 수식하는 자리에는 형용사가 옵니다. 부사는 동사, 형용사, 다른 부사를 수식할 수 있지만 명사를 수식할 수 없습니다.

questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 [조건]에 맞게 영작하시오. (영어로)
"가르침은 사회 자체가 요구하는 바를 반영한다."
[조건] (1) demands, itself, reflects, society, Teaching, what를 모두 사용
(2) 정확히 6단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: 가르침은 사회 자체가 요구하는 바를 반영한다.
det.analysis: 주어 Teaching + 동사 reflects + 관계대명사 what이 이끄는 명사절 what society itself demands의 구조. 관계대명사 what은 선행사를 포함하여 '~하는 것'이라는 의미이며, itself는 society를 강조하는 재귀대명사로 주어 뒤에 위치한다.
det.tip: what은 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사로 'the thing which'와 같습니다. 재귀대명사 itself는 강조 용법으로 앞의 명사 바로 뒤에 놓입니다.

✅ ② outer(외부의): 학생이 경험해야 하는 질서가 '외부의' 질서라는 문맥으로 적절

✅ ④ develop(발달하다): 내적 질서가 '발달한다'는 문맥으로 적절
det.tip: outer order(외부 질서) → inner order(내적 질서)라는 방향성이 본문 도입부의 핵심 논리입니다.

det.korean: 거울을 보고, 방향지시등으로 신호를 보내고, 기어 변속 전에 클러치를 밟는 것과 같은 행동들이 명시적으로 점검된다. 몇 시간의 연습 후에 운전에 필요한 행동들은 제2의 천성이 되어, 거의 모든 차량에 옮겨갈 수 있고 명시적 사고 없이 수행된다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① pressing: 병렬 구조(looking, signaling, pressing)에서 동명사로 일관되게 사용되어 올바른 어법
✅ ② are: 주어 'each required action and sequence of actions'는 and로 연결된 복수 주어이며, 뒤에 '~ are explicitly thought of and double-checked'로 복수 동사가 와서 올바른 어법
✅ ③ transferable: 주격 보어 second nature를 추가 설명하는 형용사로 올바른 어법
❌ ④ performing → performed: 앞의 transferable과 and로 병렬 연결되며 주어 the required actions가 '수행되는' 수동 의미이므로 과거분사 performed가 와야 함. 현재분사 performing은 능동 의미로 부적절
det.tip: 병렬 구조에서는 연결되는 두 요소의 품사·형태가 일치해야 합니다. 주어와 수동 관계이면 과거분사(V-ed)가 옵니다.

questions.passage: [2번] When we lecture, scold, yell, or criticize, when we say something positive but in a sarcastic tone, or when we try to make our kids feel guilty, it activates their amygdala, triggering their stress response and putting them into a defensive, rigid, reactive state. Even more basic, when we say no or don't, it releases __________ in our kids' brains (and in ours) that are associated with fear and anger. Functional brain imaging research has shown that even seeing the word no on a screen for less than a second while you're lying in an MRI scanner will cause your brain to suddenly release dozens of stress-producing hormones and neurotransmitters. Conversely, positive words like yes, love, and peace activate systems in the prefrontal cortex that are related to emotional regulation. The problem is that negative words like no and don't have a more powerful effect on kids than positive words. For this reason, the researchers Suniya Luthar and John Gottman say that "bad is stronger than good" when it comes to communicating with children and teens.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 우리가 'no'나 'don't'라고 말할 때, 그것은 아이들 뇌에서 두려움·분노와 관련된 _______ 을 분비시킨다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① positive words: 부정어의 생리적 작용을 설명하는 문맥에서 정반대 개념이므로 부적절
❌ ② negative words: 빈칸 자리에는 'release의 목적어(=분비되는 실체)'가 와야 하므로 말 자체(단어)는 부적절
✅ ③ stress chemicals: 'it releases ____ in our kids' brains ... that are associated with fear and anger'의 빈칸으로 부정어가 분비시키는 화학물질로 적절
❌ ④ stress response: 반응(response)은 결과이지 분비 대상이 아니므로 release의 목적어로 부적절
det.tip: release(분비하다)의 목적어로 올 수 있는 생리학적 실체를 고르세요. fear and anger와 연관되는 것이 단서입니다.

questions.passage: [1번] Teaching reflects what society itself demands; it necessitates that disorder — of students and teachers alike, of mind, behavior, and environment — yield to its opposite. Effective teaching requires that, failing their own self-imposed order, students experience the imposition of some outer order so that inner order may develop. This means in practice, for instance, that the goals of classes and courses be clearly set, that they be explained and justified, that the manner of achieving them be clear, that the presentation of materials conducive to reaching them be appropriate, and that all activities be directed somehow to their attainment. It means, too, that students take up their own obligation to maintain the conditions under which learning occurs: quiet in their classrooms, respect for and courtesy toward others, civility of language and behavior, and the like. Above all, it implies structured industry — study and activity that are oriented toward a goal and pursued with perseverance and method. That is, good teaching requires that teachers and students subject themselves to external and internal control so that learning can take place.
questions.stem: 본문에 따르면 수업의 목표와 그 달성 방법은 학생들에게 명시적으로 제시될 필요가 없다.

det.korean: 본문 중반에 수업 목표가 명확히 설정되고 설명되며 그 달성 방법도 분명해야 한다고 서술되어 있습니다.
det.analysis: ❌ F: 본문에 'the goals of classes and courses be clearly set, that they be explained and justified, that the manner of achieving them be clear'라고 나와 있어 목표와 달성 방법 모두 명확하게 제시되어야 함. '필요 없다'는 진술은 사실과 반대
det.tip: clearly set / explained / justified / clear 등 '명확함'을 강조하는 표현이 연속으로 등장합니다.

questions.passage: [Gateway] The purpose of class discussions ①<u>is</u> to encourage you to be an active participant, not a passive recorder. Much of the emphasis in a discussion is on getting students involved in thinking, reacting, and responding. These are important intellectual activities in the learning process, for through them you are supposed to discover and express your opinions. Writing is an invaluable tool for accomplishing these tasks. Unfortunately, too many times, when class discussion begins, pens and pencils go down. Admittedly, it is considerably more ②<u>difficult</u> to take notes from discussions than from lectures, for, unlike lectures, discussions ③<u>tend</u> to be disorganized and difficult to follow. Also, students usually don't know how much of what other students are ④<u>say</u> is important. And if you are an active participant, it is not easy to take notes and formulate what you want to say. But note taking in discussions is not only manageable, it is also important. Note taking helps to keep you active and alert; it allows you to impose some organization on the discussion; and it can prepare you to speak.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 토론에서 필기하는 것은 강의에서보다 상당히 더 어려운데, 강의와는 달리 토론은 정돈되지 않은 경향이 있고 따라가기 어렵기 때문이다. 또한 학생들은 대개 다른 학생들이 말하는 것 중 얼마만큼이 중요한지 모른다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① is: it is considerably more difficult 구조에서 가주어 it에 대한 be동사로 올바른 어법
✅ ② difficult: to follow를 수식받는 형용사 보어로 올바른 어법
✅ ③ tend: 주어 discussions(복수)에 대한 복수 동사 tend로 올바른 어법
❌ ④ say → saying: 진행형 are saying의 현재분사 자리이므로 saying이 와야 함. what other students are saying(다른 학생들이 말하고 있는 것)에서 동사원형 say는 부적절 ←정답
det.tip: be동사(are) 뒤에 본동사가 오면 현재분사(V-ing) 또는 과거분사(V-ed) 형태여야 합니다.

questions.passage: [3번] The experiences of learning to ride a bicycle or drive a car illustrate well how the "what" and "how" systems — those involved in object identification and practical action — might interact during development. When we learn to drive a car, we go through a first stage where each required action and sequence of actions — such as looking in the mirror, signaling with the blinker, pressing the clutch prior to shifting into gear, and so forth — are explicitly thought of and double-checked while monitoring our situation in the environment. ①<u>Once learning</u> and after a few hours of practice, the required actions for driving become second nature, transferable to almost any vehicle and performed without explicit thinking. Information appears to be perceived directly; the affordances of the road, the car, and the traffic implicitly detected. Actually, this sort of automatization of conscious learning can be jeopardized by the return of explicit awareness. If you start to think too much about your driving, you actually increase your chances of having an accident. People in sport competitions ②<u>confirm</u> ③<u>that</u> self-consciousness is one's worst enemy: tennis, golf, or billiard players commonly report that they lose their "touch" ④<u>by thinking</u> too much about their moves.

det.korean: 본문은 부정적인 말이 긍정적인 말보다 더 강력한 효과를 미친다고 명시하고 있습니다. 선지 ③은 그와 정반대입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 'when we lecture, scold, yell ... it activates their amygdala'와 일치
✅ ② 'positive words ... activate systems in the prefrontal cortex'와 일치
❌ ③ 본문에 'negative words ... have a more powerful effect on kids than positive words'라고 되어 있어 부정어가 더 강력함. 긍정어가 더 강력하다는 진술은 사실과 반대
✅ ④ 마지막 문장 'bad is stronger than good' 인용과 일치
det.tip: more powerful effect의 주어가 negative words인지 positive words인지 정확히 파악하세요.

ch: 야단이나 비꼬는 어조는 아이의 편도체를 자극한다
긍정적인 말은 전두엽 피질의 시스템을 활성화시킨다
긍정적인 말이 부정적인 말보다 아이에게 더 강력한 효과를 미친다
Luthar와 Gottman은 아이와의 의사소통에서 나쁜 것이 좋은 것보다 강하다고 말한다
